quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When a bus is signaling to re-enter the main road after a stop, what must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a bus that is signaling to enter the main road after stopping. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely re-enter traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: T intersection.
Lane shifting.
Side road.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: T intersection.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells you that a T intersection is ahead. Be ready to turn left or right.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Immediately pull all the way off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm. Take your foot off the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road with both hands on the wheel. Use a small turn of the steering wheel. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slowly reduce speed to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slowly reduce speed to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to see if someone is tailgating or approaching too fast. If a car is following you too closely, slow down gradually to let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Don't drink if you will drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.
Hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: How can you avoid having to make emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive in the right lane only.
Drive slower than traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems without emergency braking. This helps prevent vehicles behind you from crashing into you.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, you should:

options.text: Gradually slow down while checking your rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal your turn 3 to 5 seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror and gradually slow down. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes worse.
You become less alert.
You relax and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You relax and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, changes how you judge speed and distance, reduces your ability to see in headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks. It does not help you concentrate.

questions.question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign warns you about:

options.text: Road conditions or hazards ahead.
Cities and towns ahead.
Traffic laws and rules.
Road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions or hazards ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with yellow backgrounds and black symbols. They tell you about conditions or hazards on or near the road.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving compared to other factors?

options.text: The same way alcohol does.
The same way amphetamines do.
The same way anger does.
The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way alcohol does.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol affect driving similarly. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving about as much as a 0.05% blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours impairs driving about as much as a 0.10% blood alcohol level.

questions.question: You feel angry after an incident at work. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before you start driving home.
Stop at a bar and have a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before you start driving home.
questions.explanation: You should always cool down before driving when you are upset or angry. Driving while emotional is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: A driver behind you wants to pass. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Stay at the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and quickly.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and quickly.
questions.explanation: When a driver wants to pass you, slow down. This gives them enough room to pass safely in less time.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Use tires with the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water on the road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase your risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles, motorcycles, and bicycles. Also increase it when exiting an expressway, in bad weather, or if someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you with bright headlights. What should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look away toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
You may see more pedestrians ahead.
A reduced speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: A reduced speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: An "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed limit for a school zone ends. Always follow the school zone speed limit during the times shown.

questions.question: Your blind spot is an area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head.
Can see directly behind your vehicle.
Can see in your rearview mirror.
Can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without moving your head. They are located on the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what is the safest way to get home?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Wait 30 minutes and then drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to ride home with someone who is not drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol's effects. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what is most important?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Also use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you must:

options.text: Slow down at the light.
Drive carefully without stopping.
Merge to the right.
Stop completely before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Let other traffic and pedestrians pass first. Then go when it is safe. At railroad crossings, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices turn off before crossing.

questions.question: On long trips, how can you stay awake while driving?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Drive slower.
Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
Move your eyes side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: Take regular breaks on long drives. Stop and rest, even if you do not feel tired yet. This helps prevent drowsiness.

questions.question: When you approach railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Not worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be prepared to stop. A train or another vehicle may be using the tracks.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop. Then go when it is safe. A stop sign may also be posted at this location.

questions.question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through it means:

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
An action is not allowed.
Some drivers must yield to other drivers.
Drivers should go slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Some regulatory signs forbid certain actions. These signs are rectangular, white, with red and black symbols. A red circle with a slash over a black symbol means that action is forbidden.
